content.title: Triangle Angles, Congruence, and Similarity
content.overview: This guide covers core geometric properties of triangles for the SAT, including the Interior Angle Sum Theorem, the Exterior Angle Theorem, and criteria for determining triangle congruence and similarity. Mastering these concepts is fundamental to solving complex geometry problems.
learning_objectives: Calculate unknown interior and exterior angles of a triangle.
Identify and apply criteria for triangle congruence.
Use properties of similar triangles to solve for side length ratios and angles.

sections.title: Angle Relationships in Triangles
sections.content: 1. **Interior Angle Sum Theorem**: The sum of the three interior angles of any triangle is always $180^\circ$. 2. **Exterior Angle Theorem**: An exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles. An exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle are supplementary (sum to $180^\circ$).

sections.title: Congruent Triangles
sections.content: Congruence means two triangles have exactly the same shape and size. Common criteria for determining congruence include: SSS (three sides equal), SAS (two sides and the included angle equal), ASA (two angles and the included side equal), and AAS (two angles and a non-included side equal). In right triangles, there is also HL (hypotenuse and one leg equal).

sections.title: Similar Triangles
sections.content:
Similarity means two triangles have the same shape but may differ in size. The most common method to prove similarity is AA (two angles are equal). Properties of similar triangles: 1. Corresponding angles are equal; 2. Corresponding sides are proportional. If Triangle A is similar to Triangle B with a side length ratio of $k$, then the ratio of their areas is $k^2$.

![Similar Triangles Problem-Solving Process](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/3b03b922-5470-499e-a762-5c9dda37af11-1786502103591-394.webp)

worked_examples.question: In triangle ABC, angle A = $45^\circ$ and the exterior angle at vertex B is $110^\circ$. Find the measure of angle C.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Use the exterior angle property. The exterior angle at B equals angle A + angle C. Step 2: Substitute the known values, $110^\circ = 45^\circ + \text{angle C}$. Step 3: Solve the equation, $\text{angle C} = 110^\circ - 45^\circ = 65^\circ$.

worked_examples.question: Given that right triangle ABC is similar to right triangle DEF. If AB = 3, BC = 4 (where BC is a leg), and DE = 9 (where DE corresponds to AB), find the length of EF.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Determine the similarity ratio. The ratio of corresponding sides DE to AB is $9 / 3 = 3$. Step 2: Use the property that corresponding sides of similar triangles are proportional. $EF / BC = 3$. Step 3: Calculate $EF = 4 \times 3 = 12$.

common_mistakes: Incorrectly assuming the area ratio of similar triangles equals the side length ratio, when it is actually the square of the side length ratio.
When applying the Exterior Angle Theorem, mistakenly equating the exterior angle to the adjacent interior angle instead of the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles.
Incorrectly using SSA (two sides and a non-included angle) to prove congruence, which does not guarantee that triangles are congruent.
exam_tips: The SAT frequently tests similar triangles created by transversals of parallel lines (such as 'A-shaped' or 'X-shaped' figures); look for equal vertical angles or alternate interior angles to prove AA similarity.
If a problem states two triangles are similar and involves area, prioritize using the squared relationship of the similarity ratio.
When you see similar right triangles, remember that Pythagorean triples (3-4-5, 5-12-13, etc.) can help you quickly find missing side lengths.
content.recap: Mastering the $180^\circ$ interior angle sum, the exterior angle theorem, AA similarity criteria, and the proportionality of corresponding sides in similar triangles is key to tackling SAT geometry questions.

knowledge_claims.content: The sum of the three interior angles of any triangle is always equal to 180 degrees.
An exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles.
Congruent triangles are triangles that have exactly the same shape and size, meaning all corresponding sides and angles are equal.
AA (two corresponding angles are equal) is the most common criterion for determining that two triangles are similar.
To calculate an unknown side length in similar triangles, first determine the ratio of corresponding sides (similarity ratio), then apply it to the target side.
If two triangles are similar and the ratio of their side lengths is k, then the ratio of their areas is k squared.
SSA (Side-Side-Angle) is not a valid criterion for determining triangle congruence.
In the SAS congruence criterion, the equal angle must be the included angle between the two equal sides.
An exterior angle of a triangle and its adjacent interior angle are supplementary, meaning their sum is 180 degrees.
In geometric figures containing parallel lines, AA similarity is often found by identifying equal alternate interior angles.
